fanoutqa_023020.t: Doug McMillon :: Career :: Walmart International (2009–2013) :: chunk_0002
fanoutqa_023020.x:
Doug McMillon :: Career :: Walmart International (2009–2013) :: chunk_0002
Walmart officials moved McMillon from his role at Sam's Club to lead Walmart's international division in February 2009,[[15]](#cite_note-Jopson13-2-15) replacing [Mike Duke](/wiki/Mike_Duke "Mike Duke"), who was promoted to CEO of Walmart Stores, Inc.[[13]](#cite_note-Nisen13-13) Under McMillon, Walmart International focused on improving in existing markets, such as [Canada](/wiki/Canada "Canada"), [China](/wiki/China "China"), [United Kingdom](/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") and the [Americas](/wiki/Americas "Americas").[[16]](#cite_note-WohlMartell12-16) One area of particular importance to McMillon was integrating Walmart's "everyday low prices" model to these international markets.[[16]](#cite_note-WohlMartell12-16) Under McMillon, the international division acquired a majority stake in South Africa's Massmart Holdings Ltd. for [US$](/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")2.4 billion.[[7]](#cite_note-OKeefe15-7)[[17]](#cite_note-Maylie12-17)

During McMillon's tenure, Walmart International's sales growth outpaced Walmart US[[18]](#cite_note-Rubin13-18) and grew to 29 percent of total sales company-wide.[[13]](#cite_note-Nisen13-13) When McMillon first became head of the division, it comprised more than 3,300 stores in 14 countries.[[19]](#cite_note-Painter09-2-19) When Walmart announced it would move him to head Walmart Stores, Inc. in late 2013, Walmart International operated 6,300 stores in 26 countries.[[20]](#cite_note-Rudarakanchana-20)

Sahara :: Climate :: Temperature :: part 01 :: chunk_0003
The sky is usually clear above the desert, and the [sunshine duration](/wiki/Sunshine_duration "Sunshine duration") is extremely high everywhere in the Sahara. Most of the desert has more than 3,600 hours of bright sunshine per year (over 82% of daylight hours), and a wide area in the eastern part has over 4,000 hours of bright sunshine per year (over 91% of daylight hours). The highest values are very close to the theoretical maximum: a value of 4,300 hours, representing 98% of the total number of daylight hours per year, has been recorded both in [Upper Egypt](/wiki/Upper_Egypt "Upper Egypt") ([Aswan](/wiki/Aswan "Aswan"), [Luxor](/wiki/Luxor "Luxor")) and in the Nubian Desert ([Wadi Halfa](/wiki/Wadi_Halfa "Wadi Halfa")).[[20]](#cite_note-books.google.fr-20) The annual average direct [solar irradiation](/wiki/Solar_irradiance "Solar irradiance") is around 2,800 kWh/(m2 year) in the Great Desert. The Sahara has a huge potential for solar energy production.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/Algeria_Sahara_Desert_Photo_From_Drone_5.jpg/250px-Algeria_Sahara_Desert_Photo_From_Drone_5.jpg)](/wiki/File:Algeria_Sahara_Desert_Photo_From_Drone_5.jpg)

[Sand dunes](/wiki/Sand_dunes "Sand dunes") in the [Algerian](/wiki/Algeria "Algeria") Sahara

The high position of the Sun, the extremely low relative humidity, and the lack of [vegetation](/wiki/Vegetation "Vegetation") and rainfall make the Great Desert the hottest large region in the world, and the hottest place on Earth during summer in some spots. The average high temperature exceeds 38 to 40 °C (100.4 to 104.0 °F) during the hottest month nearly everywhere in the desert except at very high altitudes. fanoutqa_007148.x:
Google :: part 02 :: chunk_0001
Google was founded in 1998 by American computer scientists [Larry Page](/wiki/Larry_Page "Larry Page") and [Sergey Brin](/wiki/Sergey_Brin "Sergey Brin"). Together, they own about 14% of its publicly listed shares and control 56% of its stockholder voting power through [super-voting stock](/wiki/Super-voting_stock "Super-voting stock"). The company went [public](/wiki/Public_company "Public company") via an [initial public offering](/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering") (IPO) in 2004. In 2015, Google was reorganized as a wholly owned subsidiary of Alphabet Inc. Google is Alphabet's largest subsidiary and is a [holding company](/wiki/Holding_company "Holding company") for Alphabet's internet properties and interests. [Sundar Pichai](/wiki/Sundar_Pichai "Sundar Pichai") was appointed CEO of Google in 2015, replacing Larry Page, who became the CEO of Alphabet. In 2019, Pichai also became the CEO of Alphabet.[[14]](#cite_note-15)

After the success of its original service, [Google Search](/wiki/Google_Search "Google Search") (often known simply as "Google"), the company has rapidly grown to offer [a multitude of products](/wiki/List_of_Google_products "List of Google products") and [services](/wiki/List_of_Google_services "List of Google services"). These products address a wide range of use cases, including email ([Gmail](/wiki/Gmail "Gmail")), navigation and mapping ([Waze](/wiki/Waze "Waze"), [Maps](/wiki/Google_Maps "Google Maps"), and [Earth](/wiki/Google_Earth "Google Earth")), cloud computing ([Cloud](/wiki/Google_Cloud_Platform "Google Cloud Platform")), [web navigation](/wiki/Web_navigation "Web navigation") ([Chrome](/wiki/Google_Chrome "Google Chrome")), video sharing ([YouTube](/wiki/YouTube "YouTube")), productivity ([Workspace](/wiki/Google_Workspace "Google Workspace")), [operating systems](/wiki/Operating_system "Operating system") ([Android](/wiki/Android_(operating_system) "Android (operating system)")

fanoutqa_015340.x:
Philippe of Belgium :: Early life :: chunk_0001
Philippe was born on 15 April 1960 at the [Belvédère Château](/wiki/Belv%C3%A9d%C3%A8re_Ch%C3%A2teau "Belvédère Château") in [Laeken](/wiki/Laeken "Laeken"), northern [Brussels](/wiki/Brussels "Brussels"). His father, [Prince Albert](/wiki/Albert_II_of_Belgium "Albert II of Belgium"), [Prince of Liège](/wiki/Prince_of_Li%C3%A8ge "Prince of Liège") (later King Albert II), was the second son of [King Leopold III](/wiki/Leopold_III_of_Belgium "Leopold III of Belgium") and a younger brother of [Baudouin](/wiki/Baudouin_of_Belgium "Baudouin of Belgium"). His mother, [Paola, Princess of Liège](/wiki/Queen_Paola_of_Belgium "Queen Paola of Belgium") (later Queen Paola), is a daughter of the Italian aristocrat [Fulco VIII, Prince Ruffo di Calabria, 6th Duke of Guardia Lombarda](/wiki/Fulco_Ruffo_di_Calabria "Fulco Ruffo di Calabria"). His mother descends from the French [House of La Fayette](/wiki/House_of_La_Fayette "House of La Fayette"), and the king is a descendant of [Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette](/wiki/Gilbert_du_Motier,_marquis_de_Lafayette "Gilbert du Motier, marquis de Lafayette"), and [Marie Adrienne Françoise de Noailles](/wiki/Adrienne_de_La_Fayette "Adrienne de La Fayette").

Philippe was [baptised](/wiki/Baptism "Baptism") one month later at the [Church of St. James on Coudenberg](/wiki/Church_of_St._James_on_Coudenberg "Church of St. James on Coudenberg") in Brussels on 17 May,[[2]](#cite_note-3) and named Philippe after his great-great-grandfather [Prince Philippe, Count of Flanders](/wiki/Prince_Philippe,_Count_of_Flanders "Prince Philippe, Count of Flanders"). His godparents were his paternal grandfather, [King Leopold III](/wiki/Leopold_III_of_Belgium "Leopold III of Belgium"), and his maternal grandmother, Donna Luisa, Princess Ruffo di Calabria.[[3]](#cite_note-4)

**Kazakhstan**,[[e]](#cite_note-20) officially the **Republic of Kazakhstan**,[[f]](#cite_note-21) is a [landlocked country](/wiki/Landlocked_country "Landlocked country") situated primarily in [Central Asia](/wiki/Central_Asia "Central Asia"), with a [portion](/wiki/European_Kazakhstan "European Kazakhstan") of its territory extending into [Eastern Europe](/wiki/Eastern_Europe "Eastern Europe").[[g]](#cite_note-23) It borders Russia to the [north and west](/wiki/Kazakhstan%E2%80%93Russia_border "Kazakhstan–Russia border"), China to the [east](/wiki/China%E2%80%93Kazakhstan_border "China–Kazakhstan border"), [Kyrgyzstan](/wiki/Kyrgyzstan "Kyrgyzstan") to the [southeast](/wiki/Kazakhstan%E2%80%93Kyrgyzstan_border "Kazakhstan–Kyrgyzstan border"), [Uzbekistan](/wiki/Uzbekistan "Uzbekistan") to the [south](/wiki/Kazakhstan%E2%80%93Uzbekistan_border "Kazakhstan–Uzbekistan border"), and [Turkmenistan](/wiki/Turkmenistan "Turkmenistan") to the [southwest](/wiki/Kazakhstan%E2%80%93Turkmenistan_border "Kazakhstan–Turkmenistan border"), and it has a coastline along the [Caspian Sea](/wiki/Caspian_Sea "Caspian Sea"). The capital is [Astana](/wiki/Astana "Astana") and the country's [largest city](/wiki/List_of_most_populous_cities_in_Kazakhstan "List of most populous cities in Kazakhstan") and principal cultural and economic center is [Almaty](/wiki/Almaty "Almaty"), which served as the capital until 1997.

Kazakhstan is the world's [ninth-largest country by land area](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area "List of countries and dependencies by area") and the largest landlocked country. [Hilly plateaus](/wiki/Steppe "Steppe") and plains account for nearly half its vast territory, with [lowlands](/wiki/Upland_and_lowland "Upland and lowland") composing another third; its southern and eastern frontiers are composed of mountainous regions. As of May 2025, OPEC has 11 member countries: four in the [Middle East](/wiki/Middle_East "Middle East") ([West Asia](/wiki/West_Asia "West Asia")), six in [Africa](/wiki/Africa "Africa"), and one in South America.[[197]](#cite_note-197) According to the U.S. [Energy Information Administration](/wiki/Energy_Information_Administration "Energy Information Administration") (EIA), OPEC's combined rate of oil production (including [gas condensate](/wiki/Natural-gas_condensate "Natural-gas condensate")) represented 44% of the world's total in 2016,[[198]](#cite_note-EIA_Production-198) and OPEC accounted for 81.5% of the world's "proven" oil reserves. Subsequent reports from 2022 indicate that OPEC member countries were then responsible for about 38% of total world crude oil production.[[6]](#cite_note-:4-6) It is estimated that these countries hold 79.5% of the globe's proven oil reserves, with the Middle East accounting for 67.2% of OPEC's reserves.[[8]](#cite_note-:52-8)[[9]](#cite_note-:62-9)

Approval of a new member country requires agreement by three-quarters of OPEC's existing members, including all five of the founders.[[19]](#cite_note-statute-19) In October 2015, [Sudan](/wiki/Sudan "Sudan") formally submitted an application to join,[[199]](#cite_note-199) but it is not yet a member.

The newly built [Japan National Stadium](/wiki/Japan_National_Stadium "Japan National Stadium") in Tokyo was the venue for the ceremonies and the athletics events.

Main article: [Venues of the 2020 Summer Olympics and Paralympics](/wiki/Venues_of_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_and_Paralympics "Venues of the 2020 Summer Olympics and Paralympics")

In February 2012, it was announced that Tokyo's former [National Stadium](/wiki/National_Stadium_(Tokyo,_1958) "National Stadium (Tokyo, 1958)"), the central venue for the [1964 Summer Olympics](/wiki/1964_Summer_Olympics "1964 Summer Olympics"), would undergo a ¥100 billion renovation for the [2019 Rugby World Cup](/wiki/2019_Rugby_World_Cup "2019 Rugby World Cup") and the 2020 Summer Olympics.[[98]](#cite_note-108) In November 2012, the Japan Sport Council announced it was taking bids for proposed stadium designs. Of the 46 finalists, [Zaha Hadid Architects](/wiki/Zaha_Hadid_Architects "Zaha Hadid Architects") was awarded the project, which would replace the old stadium with [a new 80,000-seat stadium](/wiki/Japan_National_Stadium "Japan National Stadium"). There was criticism of Hadid's design—which was compared to a [bicycle helmet](/wiki/Bicycle_helmet "Bicycle helmet") and regarded as clashing with the surrounding [Meiji Shrine](/wiki/Meiji_Shrine "Meiji Shrine")—and widespread disapproval of the costs, even with attempts to revise and "optimize" the design.[[99]](#cite_note-109)

In June 2015, the government announced plans to reduce the new stadium's permanent capacity to 65,000 in its athletics configuration (although with the option to add up to 15,000 temporary seats for football) as a further cost-saving measure.[[100]](#cite_note-110)[[101]](#cite_
